rows.speaker: جندب بن سفيان
rows.claim: Jundub reports that after the Prophet was ill and missed two or three nights of prayer, a woman said his devil had left him; the verses were then revealed.
rows.anchor: اشتكى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم يقم ليلتين أو ثلاثا فجاءت امرأة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative report identifies the woman who taunted the Prophet as Umm Jamil, the wife of Abu Lahab.
rows.anchor: إن المرأة التي قالت ذلك أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators say Jews asked about Dhul-Qarnayn, the People of the Cave, and the Spirit; the Prophet promised an answer the next day without saying if God wills, so revelation paused.
rows.anchor: سألت اليهود، رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ذي القرنين وأصحاب الكهف وعن الروح؟

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd says Gabriel's delay was caused by a puppy in the Prophet's house; Gabriel explained that angels do not enter a house with a dog or image.
rows.anchor: كان سبب احتباس جبريل عليه السلام عنه كون جرو في بيته

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj gives the duration of the pause in revelation as twelve days.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن جريج: اثنا عشر يوما.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas gives the duration of the pause in revelation as fifteen days.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: خمسة عشر يوما.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil gives the duration of the pause in revelation as forty days.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: أربعون يوما.

rows.speaker: المشركون
rows.claim: When the polytheists said Muhammad's Lord had abandoned and disliked him, God revealed this sura.
rows.anchor: فقال المشركون: إن محمدا ودعه ربه وقلاه، فأنزل الله تعالى هذه السورة،

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: After the pause, the Prophet said he had missed Gabriel; Gabriel said he missed him even more but was an appointed servant, and the source links this to God's command governing revelation.
rows.anchor: فقال جبريل: "إني كنت أشد شوقا [إليك] (1) ، وكلني عبد مأمور"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by the whole daytime in al-duha, as the oath sets it against night; 7:98 likewise uses duha to mean daytime.
rows.anchor: أقسم بالضحى وأراد به النهار كله، بدليل أنه قابله بالليل

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: They interpret al-duha as the time when the sun has risen high and the day is temperate in heat and cold, summer and winter.
rows.anchor: يعني وقت الضحى، وهي الساعة التي فيها ارتفاع الشمس، واعتدال النهار

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the night has come on with its darkness.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: أقبل بظلامه، وهي رواية العوفي عن ابن عباس،

rows.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Awfi's report from Ibn Abbas takes the night phrase to mean that darkness has come on.
rows.anchor: وهي رواية العوفي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الوالبي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Walibi's report from Ibn Abbas takes the night phrase to mean that it has departed.
rows.anchor: وقال الوالبي عنه: إذا ذهب، قال عطاء والضحاك: غطى كل شيء بالظلمة.

rows.speaker: عطاء والضحاك
rows.claim: Ata and al-Dahhak say night has covered everything with darkness.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء والضحاك: غطى كل شيء بالظلمة.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets the night as having become level or even.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: استوى. وقال قتادة وابن زيد: سكن واستقر

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: They say the night has become still and settled, with its darkness no longer increasing.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة وابن زيد: سكن واستقر ظلامه فلا يزداد بعد ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom layl saaj and bahr saaj describes a still night or sea.
rows.anchor: يقال: ليل ساج وبحر ساج [إذا كان ساكنا] (4) . قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's answer assures the Prophet that his Lord has neither left him since choosing him nor hated him since loving him.
rows.anchor: هذا جواب القسم، أي ما تركك منذ اختارك ولا أبغضك منذ أحبك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hardship is the Prophet's struggle against polytheists, and its accompanying ease is his eventual triumph as they submit to the truth he brought.
rows.anchor: مع الشدة التي أنت فيها من جهاد المشركين يسرا ورخاء بأن يظهرك عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the promise of ease confirms it and magnifies hope.
rows.anchor: كرره لتأكيد الوعد وتعظيم الرجاء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan reports that on revelation the Prophet announced that ease had arrived and hardship would not overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن لما نزلت هذه الآية قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says that even if hardship were inside a stone, ease would seek it out and enter; hardship cannot overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه: لو كان العسر في حجر لطلبه اليسر حتى يدخل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentators explain the saying through Arabic usage: repeated definite al-usr refers to one hardship, while repeated indefinite yusr denotes two eases.
rows.anchor: واليسر مكرر بلفظ [التنكير] (3) ، فكانا يسرين،

rows.speaker: أبو علي الحسن بن يحيى بن نصر الجرجاني
rows.claim: Al-Jurjani rejects the claim that definiteness and indefiniteness alone prove one hardship and two eases; repeating a definite noun does not force one referent and an indefinite noun two.
rows.anchor: الجرجاني صاحب "النظم" (5) تكلم الناس في قوله

rows.speaker: أبو علي الحسن بن يحيى بن نصر الجرجاني
rows.claim: Al-Jurjani illustrates his objection with the repeated phrase about a horse and a sword, which does not entail one horse but two swords.
rows.anchor: فهذا لا يوجب أن يكون الفارس واحد والسيف اثنين، فمجاز قوله:

rows.speaker: أبو علي الحسن بن يحيى بن نصر الجرجاني
rows.claim: Al-Jurjani says Quraysh mocked the Prophet's poverty and offered to make him among Mecca's richest; he grieved and thought poverty was why they denied him, so the sura's blessings and promise of wealth consoled him.
rows.anchor: أن الله بعث نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو مقل مخف، فكانت قريش تعيره بذلك، حتى قالوا: إن كان بك طلب الغنى جمعنا لك مالا

rows.speaker: أبو علي الحسن بن يحيى بن نصر الجرجاني
rows.claim: For al-Jurjani, the first ease is immediate worldly relief, fulfilled through conquest of Arabian lands and wealth, including generous gifts of camels and other grants.
rows.anchor: لا يحزنك ما يقولون فإن مع العسر يسرا في الدنيا عاجلا ثم أنجزه ما وعده،

rows.speaker: أبو علي الحسن بن يحيى بن نصر الجرجاني
rows.claim: Al-Jurjani reads the second clause as a fresh promise of an afterlife benefit for all believers; its lack of an introductory conjunction marks the new beginning.
rows.anchor: ثم ابتدأ فضلا آخر من أمر الآخرة، فقال: إن مع العسر يسرا، والدليل على ابتدائه: تعريه من الفاء والواو،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وإبراهيم وعطاء بن أبي رباح ومقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: These authorities identify the fig and olive as the familiar fruits people eat and press for oil.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، والحسن، ومجاهد، وإبراهيم، وعطاء بن أبي رباح، ومقاتل، والكلبي: هو تينكم [هذا]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fig is singled out because it is a pure fruit without seeds and resembles the fruits of Paradise.
rows.anchor: خص التين بالقسم لأنها فاكهة مخلصة لا عجم لها، شبيهة بفواكه الجنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The olive is singled out for its many benefits and as a blessed tree mentioned in a report; its fruit and oil serve for food and lighting.
rows.anchor: وخص الزيتون لكثرة منافعه، ولأنه شجرة مباركة جاء بها الحديث، وهو ثمر ودهن

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima interprets the fig and olive as two mountains.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: هما جبلان. قال قتادة:

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies the fig mountain as the one bearing Damascus and the olive mountain as the one bearing Jerusalem, named for the trees growing there.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: "التين": الجبل الذي عليه دمشق، و"الزيتون": الجبل الذي عليه بيت المقدس، لأنهما ينبتان التين والزيتون.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the two words as two mosques in Syria.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هما مسجدان بالشام.

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the fig as the Mosque of Damascus and the olive as the Mosque of Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد: "التين": مسجد دمشق، و"الزيتون": مسجد بيت المقدس.

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab identifies the fig as the mosque of the People of the Cave and the olive as the Mosque of Iliya.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: "التين" مسجد أصحاب الكهف، و"الزيتون": مسجد إيليا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mount Sinai is the mountain where God spoke to Moses; the commentary refers to its mention at 23:20.
rows.anchor: يعني الجبل الذي كلم الله عليه موسى عليه السلام، وذكرنا معناه عند قوله: "وشجرة تخرج من طور سيناء"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure city is Mecca, where people were safe in both the pre-Islamic era and Islam.
rows.anchor: أي الآمن، يعني: مكة، يأمن فيه الناس في الجاهلية والإسلام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is created upright and in the finest form; unlike other animals, which lean face-down, a person stands tall, takes food by hand, and is adorned with intellect and discernment.
rows.anchor: أعدل قامة وأحسن صورة، وذلك أنه خلق كل حيوان منكبا على وجهه إلا الإنسان خلقه مديد القامة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first interpretation is return to old age: intellect diminishes and the body weakens; the elderly are lower in condition than the weak, chronically ill, and children.
rows.anchor: يريد إلى الهرم وأرذل العمر، فينقص عقله ويضعف بدنه، والسافلون: هم الضعفاء والزمنى والأطفال،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase asfal safilin is indefinite to encompass the whole category, as in calling someone the most generous of those standing rather than of the known group.
rows.anchor: نكرة تعم الجنس، كما تقول: فلان أكرم قائم

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah's codex reads the phrase with the definite form, asfal al-safilin.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله "أسفل السافلين"

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: They offer another interpretation: the return is to Hell, whose levels descend one below another.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن، وقتادة، ومجاهد: يعني ثم رددناه إلى النار، يعني إلى أسفل السافلين،

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the return is to Hell in the worst form, as a pig.
rows.anchor: قال أبو العالية: يعني إلى النار في شر صورة، في صورة خنزير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under the old-age interpretation, faculties and deeds cease, but believers who practiced righteousness keep receiving the record of deeds they used to perform after becoming feeble.
rows.anchor: فزالت عقولهم وانقطعت أعمالهم، فلا يكتب لهم حسنة إلا الذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that some people reached decrepit old age in the Prophet's time; the verse excused them and promised their earlier reward after their faculties were lost.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هم نفر ردوا إلى أرذل العمر على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فأنزل الله تعالى عذرهم.

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says old age does not harm a person whom God seals upon the best deeds he practiced.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة: لم يضر هذا الشيخ [كبره]

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report through Ikrima, Ibn Abbas interprets the exception as those who recited the Qur'an and says its reciter will not be returned to decrepit old age.
rows.anchor: وروى عاصم الأحول عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال: "إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayr mamnun means uncut or uninterrupted reward, since their former righteous deeds continue to be recorded for them.
rows.anchor: غير مقطوع، لأنه يكتب له كصالح ما كان يعمل.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the promised reward as reward without having to perform deeds.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك: أجر بغير عمل، ثم قال: إلزاما للحجة:

rows.speaker: عكرمة وعطاء والضحاك ومقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: They identify the spark-producing runners as horses striking stones with their hooves and making fire.
rows.anchor: الكلبي،:هي الخيل توري النار بحوافرها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the horses kindle warfare and the fire of enmity between their riders.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: هي الخيل تهيج الحرب ونار العداوة بين فرسانها.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says these are horses raiding in God's cause, then returning at night to kindle a fire and prepare food.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس: هي الخيل تغزو في سبيل الله ثم تأوي بالليل

rows.speaker: مجاهد وزيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Mujahid and Zayd interpret the sparks as men's stratagems in warfare, invoking an Arabic threat meaning that one will kindle a scheme against another.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد، وزيد بن أسلم: هي مكر الرجال، يعني رجال الحرب، والعرب تقول إذا أراد الرجل أن يمكر بصاحبه:

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab says the phrase refers to fires coming together.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: هي النيران تجتمع

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators identify the raiders at dawn as horses and their riders charging the enemy in the morning.
rows.anchor: هي الخيل تغير بفرسانها، على العدو عند الصباح، هذا قول أكثر المفسرين.

rows.speaker: القرظي
rows.claim: Al-Qurazi offers camels and riders departing Muzdalifa for Mina on the Day of Sacrifice; the pilgrimage practice is to wait until dawn.
rows.anchor: وقال القرظي: هي الإبل تدفع بركبانها يوم النحر من جمع (3) إلى منى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb al-ighara means to travel quickly, as in the saying that Thabir should shine so that the travelers may depart.
rows.anchor: والإغارة سرعة السير، ومنه قولهم: أشرق ثبير كيما نغير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Atharna means the horses raised dust at the place where they ran; the location is left unstated because the sense makes it understood.
rows.anchor: كناية عن غير مذكور، لأن المعنى مفهوم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naq'an means dust.
rows.anchor: نقعا} غبارا، والنقع: الغبار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The horses penetrate to the center of the enemy's assembled troop or battalion.
rows.anchor: فوسطن به جمعا} أي دخلن به وسط جمع العدو، وهم الكتيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms wastat, wastat with doubling, and tawassatat all mean the same thing: to enter the middle of a group.
rows.anchor: يقال: وسطت، القوم بالتخفيف، ووسطتهم، بالتشديد، وتوسطهم بالتشديد، كلها بمعنى واحد.

rows.speaker: القرظي
rows.claim: Al-Qurazi interprets the camels as entering the middle of the gathering at Mina.
rows.anchor: قال القرظي: [هي الإبل توسط بالقوم] (6) يعني جمع منى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These descriptions are the objects of the oath.
rows.anchor: [هذا موضع القسم] ، (7) أقسم الله بهذه الأشياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qari'a is a name for the Resurrection because it strikes hearts with terror.
rows.anchor: {القارعة} [اسم] (2) من أسماء القيامة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated questions about the Calamity heighten its awe and gravity.
rows.anchor: ما القارعة} تهويل وتعظيم. {وما أدراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scattered moths are small flying creatures that flutter into fire; al-mabthuth means scattered.
rows.anchor: هذا الفراش: الطير [الصغار البق، واحدها فراشة، أي: كالطير] (3) التي تراها تتهافت في النار، والمبثوث: المتفرق.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra compares the people to a swarm of locusts: at resurrection they surge into and over one another from terror, as at 54:7.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: كغوغاء الجراد، شبه 199/أالناس عند البعث بها [لأن الخلق] (4) يموج بعضهم في بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains become like wool that has been carded and fluffed.
rows.anchor: كالعهن المنفوش} كالصوف المندوف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heavy scales mean that a person's good deeds outweigh the bad.
rows.anchor: {فأما من ثقلت موازينه} رجحت حسناته [على سيئاته] (5) .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person with heavy scales lives in a pleasing life in Paradise.
rows.anchor: فهو في عيشة راضية} مرضية في الجنة.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains radiya as possessing contentment: the person is pleased with that life.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج ذات رضا يرضاها صاحبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Light scales mean that a person's evil deeds outweigh the good.
rows.anchor: {وأما من خفت موازينه} رجحت سيئاته على حسناته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His abode is the Fire; it is called a mother because people naturally find their resting place with their mothers.
rows.anchor: مسكنه النار، سمي المسكن أما لأن الأصل في السكون إلى الأمهات،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hawiya is a name for Hell and means a chasm whose bottom cannot be reached.
rows.anchor: والهاوية اسم من أسماء جهنم، وهو المهواة لا يدرك قعرها،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Arabs use hawat ummuhu of someone who has fallen into a grave predicament.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: وهي كلمة عربية تقولها العرب للرجل إذا وقع في أمر شديد،

rows.speaker: قتادة وأبو صالح
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes ummuhu as his head: they plunge into the Fire headfirst, upside down.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ["فأمه هاوية"] أراد أم رأسه ["منحدرة منكوسة"] يعني أنهم يهوون في النار على رءوسهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ma hiya refers to al-Hawiya; the final h was added to ma hiya for a pause and ease of stopping.
rows.anchor: يعني الهاوية، وأصلها: ما هي، أدخل الهاء فيها للوقف والاستراحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire is intensely hot, having reached the limit of heat.
rows.anchor: فقال: {نار حامية} أي حارة قد انتهى حرها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-takathur is rivalry and boasting in wealth and numbers that distracts people from obeying God and escaping His anger.
rows.anchor: شغلتكم المباهاة والمفاخرة والمكاثرة بكثرة المال والعدد عن طاعة ربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Visiting the graves means dying and being buried in them.
rows.anchor: حتى [متم] (2) ودفنتم في المقابر.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the passage concerns Jews boasting that they outnumbered one another; the rivalry distracted them until they died astray.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: نزلت في اليهود، قالوا: نحن أكثر من بني فلان، وبنو فلان أكثر من بني فلان،

rows.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: They say two Quraysh clans, Banu Abd Manaf and Banu Sahm, competed over noblemen and numbers, then counted their dead in graves; Banu Sahm claimed more because they had been more numerous in pre-Islamic times.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل والكلبي: نزلت في حيين من قريش؛ بني عبد مناف بن قصي، وبني سهم بن عمرو، كان بينهم تفاخر،

rows.speaker: أبوه
rows.claim: The father of Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah says the Prophet explained that a person owns only what he eats, wears, or gives as charity and sends ahead.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه قال: انتهيت إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يقرأ هذه الآية: "ألهاكم التكاثر"، قال:

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك عن رسول الله
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's saying that three follow the dead, but family and wealth return while the person's deeds remain.
rows.anchor: أنس بن مالك يقول: قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets al-asr as time or the ages.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: والدهر.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation says time is sworn by because it offers lessons to anyone who reflects.
rows.anchor: قيل: أقسم به لأن فيه عبرة للناظر.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the oath to mean “by the Lord of time,” as in comparable oaths.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه ورب العصر، وكذلك في أمثاله.

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan says al-asr means both night and day, which are called the two asrs.
rows.anchor: واقل ابن كيسان: أراد بالعصر الليل والنهار، يقال لهما العصران.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan identifies al-asr as the time from noon's decline until sunset.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: من بعد زوال الشمس إلى غروبها (2) .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies it as the final hour of the day.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: آخر ساعة من ساعات النهار (3) .

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil interprets the oath as the afternoon prayer, which is the middle prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: أقسم بصلاة العصر وهي الصلاة الوسطى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khusran means loss and diminution; one reported interpretation limits the human in loss to the unbeliever because believers are then excepted.
rows.anchor: قيل: أراد به [الكافر] (4) بدليل أنه استثنى المؤمنين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Loss is the destruction of a person's capital, the self and its lifetime, through sins; these are the person's greatest assets.
rows.anchor: ذهاب رأس مال الإنسان في هلاك نفسه وعمره [بالمعاصي] (5) ، وهما أكبر رأس ماله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe and do good are exempt from loss.
rows.anchor: الصالحات} فإنهم ليسوا في خسر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawaasaw means that they counsel one another.
rows.anchor: تواصوا} أوصى بعضهم بعضا،

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Hasan and Qatada say that advising one another in truth means advising one another by the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: بالحق} بالقرآن، قاله الحسن وقتادة،

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil says truth here means faith and God's oneness.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: بالإيمان والتوحيد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience means enduring in performing the obligations and upholding God's command.
rows.anchor: وتواصوا بالصبر} على أداء الفرائض وإقامة أمر الله.

rows.speaker: إبراهيم عن ابن عون
rows.claim: Ibrahim, transmitted by Ibn Awn, says aging and infirmity bring decline, except for believers whose youthful, healthy deeds continue to be recorded; this parallels 95:4–6.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن عون عن إبراهيم قال: أراد أن الإنسان إذا عمر في الدنيا وهرم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of showing off among hypocrites is linked to 4:142, where they rise for prayer lazily and for display.
rows.anchor: وقال في وصف المنافقين: "وإذا قاموا إلى الصلاة قاموا كسالى يراءون الناس"

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they neglect prayer and do not care whether they pray.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: ساه عنها لا يبالي صلى أم لم يصل.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says they neither hope for reward when praying nor fear punishment when abandoning prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا يرجون لها ثوابا إن صلوا ولا يخافون عقابا إن تركوا.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says they are heedless of prayer and treat it lightly.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: غافلون عنها يتهاونون بها.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says they pray only to be seen, and do not regret missing the prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو الذي إن صلاها صلاها رياء، وإن فاتته لم يندم.

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya says they fail to pray at the proper times and do not complete bowing and prostration.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: لا يصلونها لمواقيتها ولا يتمون ركوعها وسجودها.

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali interprets al-ma'un as the obligatory alms.
rows.anchor: روي عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه قال: هي الزكاة،

rows.speaker: ابن عمر والحسن وقتادة والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn Umar, Hasan, Qatada, and al-Dahhak also identify al-ma'un as zakat.
rows.anchor: وهو قول ابن عمر والحسن وقتادة والضحاك

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود وسعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Masud, also reported by Said ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas, identifies al-ma'un as ordinary useful things such as an axe, bucket, or pot.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود: "الماعون": الفأس والدلو والقدر وأشباه ذلك (6) وهي رواية سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets al-ma'un as a borrowed household item.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: "الماعون" [العارية. وقال

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says its greatest instance is obligatory alms and its least is lending household goods.
rows.anchor: أعلاها الزكاة المعروفة [وأدناها عارية المتاع

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب والكلبي
rows.claim: They interpret al-ma'un as good conduct and help people exchange among themselves.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب والكلبي: "الماعون": المعروف الذي يتعاطاه الناس فيما بينهم.

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub derives al-ma'un from scarcity: zakat, charity, and kindness are called small contributions from a larger amount.
rows.anchor: قال قطرب: أصل الماعون من القلة، تقول العرب: ما له: سعة ولا منعة،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says al-ma'un means things it is impermissible to withhold, such as water, salt, and fire.
rows.anchor: وقيل: "الماعون": ما لا يحل منعه مثل: الماء والملح والنار
